messages.author: 757f82d0e9848db8
messages.subject: Reactive data frame?
parts: Here's a tricky one I haven't seen asked yet. Is there a way to create a reactive data frame? I'm building an app to do analyses on data from Clinicaltrials.gov - I'll have a sidebar which is basically the search engine. Hitting "submit" downloads a set of XML files matching the search criteria. The problem is, sometimes this can take a few minutes. I would like to be able to create one data frame from this data which I can use in my analyses, and it will only update when the search is changed. Any ideas?

messages.author: 55771919c42cb6a1
messages.subject: Re: Reactive data frame?
parts:
Assuming you have a separate reactive function for retrieving the
data, you could do something roughly like this:

# Holds the downloaded data
df1 <- reactive(function() {
# Download and load the XML data
...
}

# Gets a subset based on user controls
df2 <- reactive(function() {
# Return a subset of df1(). For example, suppose min_age is
controlled by the user:
subset(df1(), age >= input$min_age)
}

output$myplot <- reactivePlot(reactivePlot(function() {
# Make the plot
...
}


-Winston
